definitions.explanation: The spreading or transmission of something (disease, culture, ideas, waves) from one place or person to another. More formal and technical than {広|ひろ}がる.

examples.japanese: {感染症|かんせんしょう}が{急速|きゅうそく}に{伝播|でんぱ}した。
{仏教|ぶっきょう}はインドから{東|ひがし}アジアに{伝播|でんぱ}した。
examples.english: Buddhism spread from India to East Asia.

examples.japanese: SNSを{通|つう}じて{情報|じょうほう}が{瞬時|しゅんじ}に{伝播|でんぱ}する{時代|じだい}になった。
examples.english: We live in an era where information spreads instantly through social media.

notes: Not to be confused with the homophone {電波|でんぱ} (radio waves). {伝播|でんぱ} is used in formal and academic writing for the spread of diseases, cultures, technologies, and ideas. In scientific contexts, it also refers to wave propagation ({音|おと}の{伝播|でんぱ} — propagation of sound). The reading でんぱ is standard; the alternative reading でんぱん is also seen but less common.
